title: UAE to India Travel: Air Suvidha 2.0, e-Arrival Card and New Gold Rules Explained
excerpt: From Ebola health screenings to revamped customs limits, here is every form and regulation UAE-based travellers need to know before flying to India in 2026.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Air Suvidha 2.0 requires health declarations for all international passengers before flying to India.
  • e-Arrival Card is mandatory for foreign nationals since April 2026, replacing paper forms.
  • New baggage rules allow ₹75,000 duty-free allowance and weight-based gold limits for travelers.
  • Gold bars and bullion are taxed from the first gram; excess personal goods now attract 10% duty.
Health Declarations and Digital Immigration
›Air Suvidha 2.0 launched on 25 June 2026.
›Mandatory health declaration for all international passengers.
›Ebola screening focus due to WHO emergency declaration.
›Form must be completed within 24 hours of departure.

Travelling from the UAE to India has never required more screen time. Between a new health portal, a mandatory digital immigration card and an overhaul of customs rules, passengers flying from Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Sharjah face a checklist that looks nothing like it did a year ago.

Air Suvidha 2.0: The Health Declaration

On 25 June 2026, the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited relaunched the Air Suvidha portal in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services. The trigger was the World Health Organization's decision in May 2026 to declare the Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

> **"Indian passport holders are exempt.

A critical detail: the system generates a QR code after submission, and closing the browser without saving it can create problems at immigration."**

This is not a relic of the COVID era. Air Suvidha 2.0 is a Self-Declaration Form focused specifically on Ebola screening. Every international passenger arriving in India — regardless of nationality, visa type or departure city — must complete the form within 24 hours of departure via the official portal at airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in. The form asks for passport details, flight information, a 21-day travel history and a health and exposure declaration.

On arrival, passengers present the downloaded form at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter. Those flagged through their travel history may be referred for further screening; most travellers clear the process in minutes.

"The official Air Suvidha portal is a free government service. Only use airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in and avoid third-party sites that charge a fee for the form."

— Indian Ministry of Civil Aviation advisory

e-Arrival Card: Digital Immigration, No More Paper

Since 1 April 2026, India's paper disembarkation form — the card passengers filled out mid-flight — has been permanently discontinued. Every foreign national and Overseas Citizen of India cardholder must now submit the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before landing.

The card collects passport details, flight information, purpose of visit and accommodation address in India. It can be completed on the Bureau of Immigration portal at indianvisaonline.gov.in or through the Su-Swagatam mobile app. Indian passport holders are exempt.

A critical detail: the system generates a QR code after submission, and closing the browser without saving it can create problems at immigration. OCI cardholders must complete both Air Suvidha and the e-Arrival Card — a point of confusion that has caught many first-time users off guard.

Gold Price Increase Since 2016

India's customs landscape shifted on 2 February 2026 when the New Baggage Rules replaced the decade-old 2016 regulations. The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs introduced three major changes that affect every UAE-based NRI packing a suitcase home.

The general duty-free allowance for personal effects climbed from ₹50,000 to ₹75,000 for Indian residents, NRIs and tourists of Indian origin who have spent more than three days abroad. Foreign tourists arriving for the first time have a separate ₹25,000 limit.

The biggest change concerns jewellery. The government scrapped value-based caps and moved to a weight-only system: women may carry up to 40 grams of gold jewellery duty-free, and other passengers may carry up to 20 grams. The old rupee caps had become unworkable after gold prices surged roughly 394 per cent since 2016, reaching ₹1,43,926 per 10 grams on the Multi Commodity Exchange by February 2026.

Gold bars, coins and bullion remain explicitly excluded and are taxable from the first gram. Excess personal-use imports now attract 10 per cent basic customs duty, replacing the earlier 20 per cent rate. Passengers must declare goods above the free limit at the Red Channel or risk confiscation and fines.

What UAE-Based Travellers Should Do

For the roughly 3.5 million Indians in the UAE — the largest expatriate community in any single country — the combined changes mean a new pre-flight routine. Fill Air Suvidha during web check-in, when Wi-Fi is reliable. Complete the e-Arrival Card separately if you hold an OCI card or foreign passport. Weigh any gold jewellery before packing; the weight limit, not the price tag, now determines whether duty applies.

Requirements during a Public Health Emergency can change at short notice. Travellers should check the Air Suvidha portal and their airline's advisories close to departure to confirm the latest rules.
